newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu closes unchanged at 3,495/3,515 to dlr.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu closes unchanged at 3,495/3,515 to dlr.

text.p: Romania's leu closed unchanged at 3,495/3,515 to the dollar on a quiet interbank market amid traders' hopes that the new government will liberalise the fx market and give banks back their lost dealer status.

"The market is dead, with no dollars, as usual. I'm confident the new government will reconsider the issue of the banks' dealer status. Under the present circumstances no one can talk about a free forex market," a trader said.
In March the BNR stripped all but four banks of their local dealer status in what it called a bid to integrate the fractured fx market. Brokers have been compelled since to observe dealers' quotes.

Over the past months, the artificially-held value of the leu has discouraged exporters from parting with their hard currency and the market was hit by inertia and chronic hard currency shortages, traders said.
Newly elected president Emil Constantinescu said the new centrist government would quickly launch reforms including liberalisation of the foreign exchange market.
Traders said those moves, expected to restore to banks their previous dealer positions, would lead to a more realistic value for the leu, now obtainable only in cross dealing.

The leu's rate at licensed money exchange offices in Bucharest on Tuesday lingered around 4,800 to the dollar "and is returning to normal" a trader said, referring to the leu's gradual firming from an all-time low 5,050 at the weekend.
"It appears there is a big accumulation of dollars on the retail market. Now everybody shouts for lei," a trader said.
One-week prices were at around 45 percent, traders said. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
